intent_record.intent_summary: Fix tunnel lookup to only match tunnels with wildcard remote addresses by adding ipv6_addr_any() check for the remote address parameter.
intent_record.what: Added a new condition `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr) &&` to the if statement in the vti6_tnl_lookup function, checking if the tunnel's remote address is the IPv6 any address before returning a matching tunnel.
intent_record.how: This change adds an additional filter criterion to the tunnel lookup logic. Previously, the function would return a tunnel matching only on local address equality and UP flag status. Now it additionally requires that the tunnel's remote address parameter be the IPv6 any address (::0). This prevents matching tunnels with specific remote addresses when searching for a fallback tunnel, ensuring only wildcard/any-address tunnels are returned in this code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix tunnel lookup to correctly match only tunnels with wildcard local addresses by adding ipv6_addr_any() check.
intent_record.what: Added a new condition `ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)` to the tunnel lookup comparison in the vti6_tnl_lookup function, placed between the remote address equality check and the IFF_UP flags check.
intent_record.how: This change adds an additional filter criterion to the tunnel selection logic. Now a tunnel is only returned as a match if not only the remote address matches and the device is up, but also if the local address (laddr) is set to any/unspecified. This prevents matching tunnels that have a specific local address configured, restricting matches to tunnels with wildcard local addresses.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.

Currently we can't lookup tunnels with wildcard endpoint
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit fbe68ee87522f6eaa10f9076c0a7117e1613f2f7
Author: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Date:   Thu Nov 20 10:01:49 2014 +0100

    vti6: Add a lookup method for tunnels with wildcard endpoints.
    
    Currently we can't lookup tunnels with wildcard endpoints.
    This patch adds a method to lookup these tunnels in the
    receive path.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
index d440bb58552
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds wildcard endpoint lookup logic to vti6_tnl_lookup(), but the implementation is missing critical validation checks. Specifically: (1) In the second loop (lines 107-110), it searches for tunnels with remote=any and local=local, but only checks if local addresses match without verifying that the retrieved tunnel actually has a wildcard remote address (t->parms.raddr should be all zeros). (2) In the third loop (lines 112-116), it searches for tunnels with remote=remote and local=any, but only checks if remote addresses match without verifying that the retrieved tunnel actually has a wildcard local address (t->parms.laddr should be all zeros). Due to hash collisions, non-wildcard tunnels could be returned from these loops and incorrectly matched. The fix would require adding explicit checks like 'ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr)' in the second loop and 'ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)' in the third loop to ensure only truly wildcard tunnels are matched.

Author: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Date:   Mon Aug 19 08:07:34 2013 +0200

    ipv6: Add support for IPsec virtual tunnel interfaces
    
    This patch adds IPv6  support for IPsec virtual tunnel interfaces
    (vti). IPsec virtual tunnel interfaces provide a routable interface
    for IPsec tunnel endpoints.
    
    Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c b/net/ipv6/ip6
bic_trace_step.reason: The vti6_tnl_lookup() function (lines 115-130) contains the vulnerable construct. It performs a hash-based lookup in tnls_r_l[hash] for exact matches, then falls back to checking tnls_wc[0] (wildcard tunnel) without validating that the fallback tunnel actually has wildcard addresses. The code at lines 127-129 shows: 't = rcu_dereference(ip6n->tnls_wc[0]); if (t && (t->dev->flags & IFF_UP)) return t;' - this returns the tunnel from the wildcard list without checking if it actually contains wildcard (any) addresses in laddr and raddr. This allows non-wildcard tunnels retrieved from hash collisions in the first loop to be incorrectly matched. The fix would require adding ipv6_addr_any() checks on the fallback tunnel's addresses before returning it, similar to how vti6_tnl_bucket() validates addresses at lines 152-156.

diff --git a/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c b/net/ipv6/ip6_vti.c
index d440bb58552
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds wildcard endpoint lookup logic to vti6_tnl_lookup(), but the implementation is vulnerable because it lacks validation that candidate tunnels actually have wildcard addresses. Specifically: (1) The second loop (lines 108-111) searches with hash=HASH(&any, local) but only checks if 'local' matches t->parms.laddr without verifying that t->parms.raddr is actually a wildcard (any address). (2) The third loop (lines 113-117) searches with hash=HASH(remote, &any) but only checks if 'remote' matches t->parms.raddr without verifying that t->parms.laddr is actually a wildcard. Due to hash collisions, these loops can retrieve non-wildcard tunnels from the hash table, and without explicit wildcard validation checks (e.g., ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.raddr) or ipv6_addr_any(&t->parms.laddr)), non-wildcard tunnels will be incorrectly matched and returned. The root cause condition exists: the code performs fallback searches but fails to confirm that retrieved candidates actually have wildcard addresses.
